triage.rationale: IBRANCE matches the criteria because its primary patent expiry of 2027-03-05 falls within the 2027-01-01 to 2029-12-31 window, and it is a known blockbuster oncology small molecule.

drugSummary.name: Ibrance (palbociclib)
drugSummary.mechanismOfAction: Ibrance is an inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6 (CDK4/6). By inhibiting these key regulators of the cell cycle, it can block the G1 to S phase transition, leading to a halt in cell proliferation.
indications: For the treatment of adult patients with hormone receptor (HR)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer in combination with an aromatase inhibitor as initial endocrine-based therapy.

For the treatment of adult patients with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer in combination with fulvestrant in patients with disease progression following endocrine therapy.

patentTimeline.narrative: Ibrance's market protection is anchored by its core composition-of-matter patent expiring in March 2027, which receives a six-month pediatric extension to September 2027 [1]. However, subsequent pediatric exclusivity periods provide the final barrier to entry, with the last one expiring in March 2029, defining the projected generic launch date [4]. A later-expiring patent extending to 2034 creates a patent thicket that may deter or complicate generic competition beyond this date [2].
